newsitem.title: USA: Respironics says patent charges dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Respironics says patent charges dismissed.

text.p: Respironics Inc said Wednesday that a federal court in Pennsylvania has dismissed charges that its patient masks infringe a patent held by ResMed Ltd, an Australian medical products manufacturer.
The Australian company is a unit of San Diego, Calif.,-based ResMed Inc which is involved in the diagnosis and treatment of sleep-disordered breathing.
In a statement, Respironics said that on July 2, the court adopted a recommendation made on May 28 by a U.S. magistrate judge, who found insufficient basis for ResMed's charges, Respironics said.
ResMed had charged that Respironics infringed U.S. Patent No. 5,243,971 which relates to a patient mask that ResMed refers to as the "Bubble Mask," Respironics said.
It said the court found that because of its design, the Respironics mask could not infringe the patent.
According to Respironics, ResMed started its case in 1992 by filing charges in Australia. The Australian Supreme Court ruled in Respironics' favor in 1994, it said.
ResMed then filed with U.S. courts in 1995, alleging infringements of four patents, it said.
The July 2 ruling affects one of those patents and litigation on the three others continues, a Respironics official said.
